paragraphs.5: Score Companion helps musicians turn sheet-music PDFs into measures and save difficult passages for practice. This report covers P11 launch preparation, delivery, and security. A temporary free HTTPS demo was verified through Docker; durable hosting and outside-user testing remain pending. No demo video is included. The final presentation and live demo belong to P13.

paragraphs.23: Public HTTPS URL: https://locate-valuation-using-donald.trycloudflare.com. This is a temporary free Cloudflare Quick Tunnel backed by Docker and is available only while its tunnel container runs.
paragraphs.24: The verified demo uses Docker Compose on the development computer and the free Cloudflare Quick Tunnel image. No Google Cloud VM, billing account, paid host, or billable cloud resource was provisioned.
paragraphs.25: The Docker stack retains the application database and uploaded PDFs in its named volume while it runs Java, Poppler, and Audiveris for recognition. The public check completed a real PDF conversion with 56 passages and layout version 1, then returned a 608 x 607 measure PNG over HTTPS. Recreating the application containers preserved two completed scores, 112 passages, and the source PDF. A temporary tunnel is suitable for a free demo, not a permanent production service.

paragraphs.50: Score Companion helps you focus on difficult measures.
paragraphs.51: Get it: https://locate-valuation-using-donald.trycloudflare.com while the free Docker tunnel is running. The address is temporary and may change after restart.
paragraphs.53: Open the library and upload a clear sheet-music PDF you have permission to use. Wait for measure extraction, then open the score and select a measure.
paragraphs.54: Save the measure with a practice note. Open Practice Review, mark it practiced, and return to the passage. Remove a saved practice item or uploaded score when no longer needed.
paragraphs.55: Questions and defects: use the repository issue tracker. Browser libraries are private sessions; deleting an uploaded score removes its owned file and records.
paragraphs.57: Part 3 CI and CD for launch
paragraphs.58: Pipeline configuration: root .gitlab-ci.yml is present. GitLab is the authoritative delivery platform; GitHub remains a mirror.
paragraphs.59: Required behavior: validate branches and merge requests; deploy an approved protected main build only after required checks succeed.
paragraphs.60: Required jobs are defined for Django checks and backend tests; frontend lint, tests, and production build; dependency scans; gated deployment; and post-deployment health verification. No paid deployment job was enabled.
paragraphs.61: Secrets: local OAuth files are excluded from Git and Docker builds. Deployment identity and any CI variables must be configured securely for the chosen host. No secret values belong in this report or the frontend bundle.
paragraphs.62: Pipelines for merge requests !30 and !31 failed before jobs were created. The second used online free ULL group runners, but GitLab still requires account identity verification. Static CI lint passed; no successful pipeline, paid runner, or deployment is claimed.
paragraphs.66: The default local demo profile remains available for development, while the free public overlay enables server-controlled browser sessions and a private library.
paragraphs.67: Controls include server session identity, ownership checks, protected PDF and image routes, CSRF, secure cookies, upload limits, and bounded recognition. The 54 backend tests, 24 frontend tests, production checks, Docker health, public measure, restart-persistence, and two-session isolation checks passed.
